slot.brief: A wheel rolls without slipping at a given speed; find the speed or direction of a point on the rim at a specified position (top, side, or at a stated angle).

stem: A wheel rolls without slipping to the right with its centre moving at $4$ m s$^{-1}$. What is the speed of a point at the rightmost edge of the rim?

verdicts.working: For rolling without slipping, the rim’s rotational speed is 4 m s⁻¹. At the rightmost point it is perpendicular to the centre’s 4 m s⁻¹ velocity, so the resultant speed is √(4² + 4²) = 4√2 m s⁻¹.

working:
At the rightmost point, $v_{\text{rot}}=v_{\text{cm}}=4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, perpendicular to $v_{\text{cm}}$.
$v=\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=4\sqrt{2}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ Independent check: For rolling without slipping, the rim’s rotational speed is 4 m s⁻¹. At the rightmost point it is perpendicular to the centre’s 4 m s⁻¹ velocity, so the resultant speed is √(4² + 4²) = 4√2 m s⁻¹.
solution:
For rolling without slipping, the rotational speed of the rim is $v_{\text{cm}}=4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. At the rightmost point, this velocity is perpendicular to the centre’s velocity, so
$$v=\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=4\sqrt{2}\ \text{m s}^{-1}.$$
